explanation: To solve log_b(x) = C you undo the log by raising the base to each side: x = b^C. The blue curve is y = log_b(x) and the purple line is the target y = C; where they cross is the solution x, found by dropping straight down to the x-axis. The yellow dot rides the slow-growing log curve so you can see how far right you must go for the log to reach the value C.
bullets: log_b(x) = C is undone by exponentiating: x = b^C.
Graphically x is where the curve y = log_b(x) meets the line y = C.
Always check the answer is positive — a log is only defined for x > 0.
